SMTO-LLM-0022 — The model service didn't accept SMTO's sign-in

GUID: eef9863a-43f4-435b-bbe7-61918b138270
Slug: provider-authentication-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model service turned down SMTO's request because it couldn't confirm who was asking. Nothing from this request was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and open the Main card. If it shows API key missing, enter the key again, or tick Use no API key if this server needs none. A missing key is the simplest cause, and the card warns you when the saved key is gone.
  2. Confirm the Endpoint is the service your key belongs to. If your provider says the key has changed, enter the new one and select Save Main. A key only works with the service and account that issued it.
  3. Select Check saved model, and when it passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The test confirms the service now accepts SMTO, and the rejected request did nothing that needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages your model service account whether the key is still active and allowed to use this model, and send them the copied error details. Never paste your API key into a chat or an error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider rejected the request's authentication (HTTP 401, provider_authentication_rejected); the failed call authorized no operation.

What this means

  • This category includes HTTP 401 and HTTP 403. A 401 concerns authentication; a 403 establishes access rejection and may involve account permissions or endpoint policy. Neither the broad category nor a 403 alone proves that a password is incorrect.

Why this can happen

  • The provider returned an authentication or authorization rejection. The account, credential validity and policy must be checked separately.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the recorded HTTP status. For 401, verify the configured authentication method and credential validity. For 403, check the intended account, allowed model and provider policy before replacing credentials.

How to fix it

  • Check http_status, llm_base_url and llm_model in provider_diagnostic. Verify the role's API key is present and belongs to that endpoint's account, for example with an authenticated GET of the endpoint's /models. Replace the credential only after confirming it is invalid or revoked; a 401 alone does not prove which part of the sign-in is wrong.
  • Ask the provider operator to check the recorded status, intended account and model access. Replace credentials only when their invalidity is established.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account can submit an authorized request to the selected model.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Status classification describes this model request and grants no authority to replay earlier tools.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
